title: Insert at the front
summary: Why the new node is linked first and head is moved second.

checkpoints.text: The list starts empty: `head` is NULL.
A new node exists but is not part of the list yet. It is drawn below its future place, with a dashed border, and its `next` shows `?` because it has no value.
The new node now points at the old first node, so it moves up into the row. `head` has not changed yet: it still points at the old first node.
Now `head` points at the new node. Because `head` is a reference parameter (`Node*& head`), this changes the `head` in `main`.
If the two assignments were swapped, `head = n;` would run first and the old list would be lost before `n->next` could point at it.
